skill.name: tdd-workflow
skill.description: Apply test-driven development through the Red-Green-Refactor cycle, focused tests, minimal implementations, and incremental code improvement.
skill.summary: Guide coding work with practical test-first development principles.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by ordinary TDD prose and a fenced process diagram. No executable commands, reconnaissance behavior, or prompt injection were found.

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 17-25 are a fenced text diagram of the Red-Green-Refactor cycle. They contain no Ruby code, shell command, or command execution instruction.
Line 45 gives a test-name example for invalid data. The word "throw" describes expected error behavior and does not request system reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Unstructured coding often produces unverified behavior and costly rework. This skill guides development through focused failing tests, minimal implementations, and disciplined refactoring.
actual_capabilities: Structures coding tasks around the Red-Green-Refactor cycle.
Guides creation of focused tests for expected behavior, errors, and edge cases.
Encourages minimal production code during the Green phase.
Applies Arrange-Act-Assert structure to individual tests.
Prioritizes happy paths, error cases, edge cases, and performance tests.
Supports separate agent roles for testing, implementation, and refactoring.
limitations: Provides workflow guidance rather than framework-specific test syntax.
Does not run tests or verify repository behavior independently.
Offers limited value for exploratory prototypes and visual layout work.
Requires clear requirements before a meaningful failing test can be written.

use_cases.title: Develop a New Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a feature requirement into focused tests, minimal implementation steps, and controlled refactoring.

use_cases.title: Prevent Bug Regressions
use_cases.description: Reproduce a defect with a failing test before implementing and refining the correction.

use_cases.title: Coordinate AI Coding Roles
use_cases.description: Assign test writing, implementation, and refactoring responsibilities across separate AI agents.

prompt_templates.title: Start a TDD Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through Red-Green-Refactor for this requirement: [requirement]. Begin with one observable behavior and a failing test.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner is implementing a small, well-defined behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Bug Test First
prompt_templates.prompt: Use TDD to fix this defect: [defect]. First define a regression test, then propose the smallest correction.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs to correct a reproducible defect.

prompt_templates.title: Design Edge Case Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [feature] and prioritize happy-path, error, and edge-case tests. Organize each test using Arrange, Act, and Assert.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs systematic behavioral coverage before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Multi-Agent TDD Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a multi-agent TDD workflow for [complex feature]. Separate Red, Green, and Refactor responsibilities with review gates and acceptance criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: A technical lead coordinates advanced AI-assisted development.

output_examples.input: Add rejection of empty email addresses using TDD.
output: Red: Add a focused test expecting empty email input to be rejected.
Green: Add the minimum validation needed to satisfy that test.
Refactor: Clarify validation names while preserving all passing tests.

output_examples.input: Fix a calculator defect where division by zero returns an invalid value.
output_examples.output: First reproduce the defect with an error-focused test. Then add the smallest guard and simplify only after the full suite passes.

output_examples.input: Prioritize tests for a new order total calculation.
output: Priority 1: Verify a standard order total.
Priority 2: Verify invalid prices and quantities.
Priority 3: Verify empty orders and rounding boundaries.
Priority 4: Measure performance for large orders.

best_practices: Confirm every new test fails for the expected reason before implementation.
Keep each test focused on one observable behavior.
Refactor in small steps while the complete test suite remains passing.
anti_patterns: Writing production code before observing a meaningful failing test.
Testing private implementation details instead of external behavior.
Adding optimization or unrelated abstractions during the Green phase.

faq.question: What development cycle does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses Red-Green-Refactor: write a failing test, implement minimal passing code, then improve the design.

faq.question: Can this skill write framework-specific tests?
faq.answer: It provides general test design guidance. The prompt must include repository and framework context for specific syntax.

faq.question: Does the skill execute tests?
faq.answer: No. It guides the workflow, while the selected coding tool and project environment handle test execution.

faq.question: When is TDD most useful?
faq.answer: It is most useful for new behavior, bug fixes, and complex logic with clear expected outcomes.

faq.question: When should TDD be limited?
faq.answer: Use exploratory spikes for uncertain ideas, then apply TDD after requirements and interfaces become clearer.

faq.question: Can multiple AI agents use this workflow?
faq.answer: Yes. Separate agents can own failing tests, minimal implementation, and refactoring, with shared acceptance criteria.
